extracted.intended_audience: third-party requesters, patent owners, and registered practitioners preparing or responding to ex parte reexamination requests before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and filing requirements for preparing, filing, and processing ex parte reexamination requests and related reexamination correspondence with the USPTO, including what must be shown to raise a substantial new question of patentability and procedural/formal requirements for submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim-by-claim explanation of proposed combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must explain how each of the proposed combinations specifically applies to each claim that it is asserted against (i.e., claim-by-claim), explaining how each document (reference) identified for the combination is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally provide an appropriately detailed claim chart that compares, limitation by limitation, each claim for which reexamination is requested with the relevant teachings of each reference cited in the request. See sample request in MPEP § 2214. Any failure to provide the required explanation for any document, combination, or claim will be identified in a Notice of Failure to Comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for combining references for obviousness rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed obviousness rejections, the requester must provide at least one basis for combining the cited references and a statement of why the claim(s) under reexamination would have been obvious over the proposed reference combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably quote the pertinent teachings in the references, referencing each quote by page, column and line number and any relevant figure numbers. The explanation must not lump together proposed rejections or proposed combinations of references. Examples of appropriate and inappropriate language are provided to illustrate specificity (e.g., avoid 'Smith and/or Charles' or 'either Jones and Cooper or Harvey and Cooper'; use specific combinations tied to specific claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid lumped/alternative language when asserting rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use language that lumps together multiple possible rejections or ambiguous alternative combinations when asserting unpatentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of inappropriate language include statements like 'anticipated by, or in the alternative, under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over the Smith reference' or 'Smith and/or Charles'. Appropriate language spells out the exact rejection and exact combination for a specific claim (e.g., 'Claim 2 is unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over Smith in view of Jones').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of affidavits/declarations and other written evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits, declarations or other written evidence which explain the contents or pertinent dates of prior art patents or printed publications may be considered in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2258 for guidance on admissibility and use of such written evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and limits of admissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissions by the patent owner of record may be utilized in combination with a patent or printed publication but an admission alone generally may not be the basis for establishing a substantial new question of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions must stand on their own; information supplementing or further defining the admission is improper. A third party may not submit admissions made outside the file or court record unless such admissions were entered into a court record and then submitted as a copy of a court filing (and even then they may not be given weight as an admission for establishing an SNQ). See Ex parte McGaughey and MPEP § 2258.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of each relied-on prior art document must be filed and legible
rubrics_metrics.description: It is required that a copy of each patent or printed publication relied on or referred to in the request be filed with the request (37 CFR 1.510(b)(3)); illegible copies are deemed not provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a copy is not legible or will not be legible when scanned into IFW, it is deemed not provided and will be identified in a Notice of Failure to Comply. Color photographs and similar color submissions that are legible as presented will be retained in an 'artifact' file. Non-English documents require an English language translation of all necessary and pertinent parts (an abstract is usually not sufficient). Note: the requirement to include copies of U.S. patents and U.S. patent publications is not currently being enforced and is deemed waived to that extent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide copies of prior art considered during original prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: It is helpful to include copies of prior art considered during earlier prosecution (via 37 CFR 1.555 IDS) in addition to the new prior art relied upon as raising a substantial new question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including both old and new prior art allows comparison to determine whether a substantial new question of patentability is present. See MPEP § 2242.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a copy of the printed patent in the request
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesters are required under 37 CFR 1.510(b)(4) to include a copy of the patent for which reexamination is requested to serve as the specification for the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a full copy of the printed patent (including front page) in double-column format so it can be used for the abstract, drawings, specification, and claims. Also include any disclaimer, certificate of correction, reexamination certificate, and copies of relevant Federal Court decisions, complaints, or interference decisions so the Office has a complete history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Service and service on patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: If the requester is a person other than the patent owner, the patent owner must be served with a copy of the request in its entirety at the patent owner’s correspondence address as indicated in 37 CFR 1.33(c). A certificate of service must be attached to the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate of service must set forth the name and address of the party served and the method of service. The copy of the request served on the patent owner must include a copy of the certificate of service. If service was not possible after reasonable effort, supply a duplicate copy to the Office with a cover letter explaining the efforts made and why unsuccessful; recommended heading language is given to label the submission as a duplicate copy filed when service was not possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner may include proposed amendments with request
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.510(e), a patent owner may include a proposed amendment with his or her request, but any such amendment must comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d) through (j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment adds claims, excess claims fees under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4) may apply. The request should be decided on the wording of the patent claims in effect at the time (without any proposed amendments); if reexamination is granted, subsequent prosecution is on the basis of claims as amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address is controlling; signature requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All notices, official letters, and other communications for the patent owner in a reexamination proceeding will be directed to the correspondence address (37 CFR 1.33(c)). Amendments and other papers filed on behalf of patent owners must be signed by the patent owner(s) or by an attorney or agent of record or a registered attorney/agent acting in a representative capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double correspondence with the patent owner and the patent owner’s attorney or agent normally will not be undertaken. Practitioners have duties under 37 CFR 10.23(c)(8) to timely notify clients or former clients of correspondence received from the Office that could significantly affect a matter pending before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of attorney or agent—timing condition
rubrics_metrics.description: A request by an attorney or agent of record to withdraw from a patent will normally be approved only if at least 30 days remain in any running period for response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample forms for withdrawal and change of correspondence address are provided (PTO/SB/83). See MPEP § 402.06 for additional context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing and routing of reexamination correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific mailing and hand-delivery addresses and Mail Stop markings are prescribed for ex parte reexamination correspondence to ensure proper routing to the Central Reexamination Unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mail Stop 'Ex Parte Reexam' to Central Reexamination Unit, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450. Hand-carried or delivery-service correspondence should be delivered to the Customer Service Window, Randolph Building, 401 Dulany Street, Alexandria, VA 22314 and also marked 'Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam'. Place Mail Stop information prominently on the first page in large font. Requests for ex parte reexamination may not be sent by fax (37 CFR 1.6(d)(5)); subsequent ex parte reexamination correspondence may be faxed to (571) 273-9900. EFS-Web may be used to submit requests and follow-on papers (effective July 9, 2007).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of proceeding in subsequent correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing a request for ex parte reexamination, any letters related to the resulting proceeding should identify the proceeding by patent number, the reexamination request control number, the art unit, and the name of the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate of mailing and transmission procedures (37 CFR 1.8) may be used to file many papers in ex parte reexamination proceedings (except the initial request and corrected/replacement requests); see MPEP §§ 512, 513 for rules on mailing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on filing merits papers prior to decision
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing a request, no papers directed to the merits of the reexamination other than (A) citations under 37 CFR 1.501 or 1.555, (B) another complete request under 37 CFR 1.510 or 1.915, or (C) notifications pursuant to MPEP § 2282 should be filed prior to the decision on the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other papers directed to the merits filed before the decision will be returned or, if entered prior to discovery of impropriety, expunged from the record. A copy of the letter providing notification of returned/expunged papers will be made of record, but the returned/expunged papers will not be retained by the Office. Such papers may be filed and accepted later in the proceedings if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing and mail opening for reexamination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Opening of mail marked 'Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam' and initial clerical processing of requests for reexamination are performed by the reexamination preprocessing staff in the Office of Patent Legal Administration, Central Reexamination Unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions to cure incomplete requests should be marked 'Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam' so they can be promptly forwarded to the preprocessing staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete request—notice and opportunity to correct
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request does not include the required fee or meet requirements, the requester will be notified and generally given an opportunity (usually 30 days) to complete the request; failure to comply can result in no filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTOL-2077 'Notice of Failure to Comply with Ex Parte Reexamination Request Filing Requirements' is used to notify requesters. If defects are not remedied, the request will not be granted a filing date and may be treated as a 37 CFR 1.501 citation. The filing date is the date the request satisfies all requirements. Typically only one opportunity is given to correct defects absent extraordinary circumstances; failure may lead to a Decision Vacating the Proceeding or vacating the assigned filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision vacating filing date and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If a non-compliance item is discovered after a filing date is assigned, the Office may issue a Decision Vacating the filing date and give requester time to correct the non-compliance; failure to correct can result in the proceeding being vacated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner forwards memos to supervisory and legal staff to confirm non-compliance. Examples include returned or stopped-payment checks discovered after filing date assignment. A single failure to comply with the Office notice ordinarily results in the request not being granted a filing date absent extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of filing in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of filing of all complete ex parte reexamination requests will be published in the Official Gazette approximately 4–5 weeks after filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both reexamination requests with filing dates and Director-initiated orders to reexamine will be announced. The notice will include the name of any requestor and other items required by 37 CFR 1.11(c). A record of requests filed is also maintained in the Patent Search Room and reexamination preprocessing area, and may be queried via PALM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive notice by publication when patent owner cannot be reached
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is not possible to deliver mail to the patent owner because no current address is available and all efforts fail, publication in the Official Gazette of the notice of filing or the ordering of reexamination will serve as constructive notice to the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings may proceed without actual notice to the patent owner in such instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing corrections to an incomplete request
rubrics_metrics.description: All processing of submissions to cure an incomplete request for ex parte reexamination is carried out in the preprocessing area of the Central Reexamination Unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such submissions should be marked 'Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam' to ensure prompt handling (see MPEP § 2224).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to reexamination files via Public PAIR and copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination files are open to public inspection via Public PAIR on the USPTO website, with the exception of non-patent literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To access Public PAIR follow the USPTO navigation steps and search by control number. Copies of the reexamination file may be ordered from Document Services Division (Mail Stop Document Services) or requested via email (dsd@uspto.gov); certified copies and CD-ROMs are available for purchase. Alternatively, copies may be obtained from IFW via PAIR.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to determine if a reexamination request was filed for a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural steps are provided for using the Internet (USPTO website) and internal systems (PALM/PAIR) to determine whether a reexamination request has been filed for a given patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance lists step-by-step navigation to the USPTO site and Public PAIR to search by control number or patent number to locate reexamination filings.
